messages:
jamie: Quick sync — product asked for a short spec on graceful degradation behavior clients should expect during capacity pressure. Wanted to float a compact hint strategy before I write the doc.

neha: Nice. Are we talking about HTTP codes only, or do we want to attach a small advisory header so SDKs can surface more actionable UI hints?

arun: Prefer header + status. Status remains canonical for programmatic flows, header provides a human-friendly category: e.g., `X-Redwood-Degrade: throttled|degraded|fallback` and `X-Redwood-Estimate: 200-800ms` for expected additional latency.

maria: +1 to header. Also want an explicit `retry-after` semantics for queueing vs hard quota. We should never overload clients with ambiguous `429` when it's actually a transient queuing scenario.

liam: question: SDKs already treat 429 as retryable. If we add `X-Redwood-Degrade: queued`, do we keep 429 or switch to 202 with polling?

arun: Keep 429 for rate-limit/soft-throttle. Use a `202` variant only for long-running burst-queue acceptance where we return an operation id and callback hook. Otherwise 429 + `X-Redwood-Degrade: queued;ETA=5s` is fine.

jamie: UX concern from prod: console needs a way to surface when clients are seeing 'graceful degrade' vs 'hard error' across routes. Telemetry needs a compact enum so dashboards can aggregate.

prod-ux: For dashboards, a 3-state enum works best: OK | DEGRADED | FAILED. DEGRADED should map to headers where `X-Redwood-Degrade` != absent. Also want a tooltip copy for each state.

neha: Telemetry fields proposal: `response_status`, `degrade_reason` (enum), `degrade_estimate_ms` (nullable int), `route_policy` (e.g., fallback|region|tier). Keep names short for ingestion.

maria: We should pin the enum values so they don't drift: degrade_reason = {capacity_pressure, model_fallback, cold_kv, quota_exceeded, maintenance}.

liam: How do we handle i18n for client-facing hint messages? Console will show english by default but SDKs might need localized strings. Maybe SDKs read code + provide localized copy.

arun: Agree — headers must be stable codes only. Any human readable message must be delivered by SDKs/localization layer; not in headers. So `X-Redwood-Degrade: capacity_pressure;code=CP01` and SDK maps CP01 -> localized copy.

jamie: Rollout plan: implement headers + telemetry in canary for 2 services (chat + embeddings), collect client SDK adoption metrics, then expand. Can we land server-side flags to toggle header emission?

deploy-bot: deploy: canary rollout started for inference-chat v2 -> 10% hosts.

maria: For consoles, add a small badge and drill-down that shows last 24h degrade_count and top reasons. Add an alert if degrade_rate > 3% for a customer route.

neha: One more: SDK backoff changes — if header present with `ETA`, SDK should apply a short adaptive backoff instead of full exponential. Add guidance to SDK docs.

liam: Sounds good. I can draft the SDK guidance and sample code for `X-Redwood-Degrade` handling (JS + Python).

jamie: Ok action items: 1) arun & neha draft minimal header and telemetry spec, 2) liam writes SDK guidance snippet, 3) prod-ux designs console badge copy and drilldown, 4) maria defines alert thresholds. I'll assemble into a short RFC. Deadline EOD Wednesday.

maria: ping on RFC draft when ready, I'll review alerts. :+1:

jamie: Thanks everyone, will drop an RFC link here when I have the first pass.

deploy-bot: reminder: canary will auto-increase after 1h if no errors detected.
